summary: All six prior findings are fixed. (1) onFullyRefunded now subtracts priorDue(SUM earn_due) after taking the per-user lock. A negative or zero remainder inserts nothing, and a replay is still a no-op through the earn-<order> reference. Per-return events that arrive after it see the earn- row and get 0 remaining, so the total stays at or below E. The new legacyAfterPerReturn test covers this. (2) roundsDown uses 26 coins and expects 8, which pins RoundingMode.DOWN against HALF_UP (that would give 9). (3) completingReturnEvent refunds three sibling returns end to end. It checks that the third return's outbox payload has paymentStatus=REFUNDED and returnItemsValue=100, and that the second's payload does not have REFUNDED. (4) The runbook and events.md now name both returnId and returnItemsValue; the runbook sentence is garbled (nit). (5) A WARN is logged for a non-completing return that has no usable orderValue. (6) The deserialiser test now goes through KafkaJson.eventDeserializer. The security fixes are sound. dueFor returns 0 for a value of zero or less, caps value at orderValue so the share is at most the total, and wraps the result in Math.max(0, ...). With the cap, intValueExact cannot overflow on a scale-0 result. The V5 CHECK constraint (all dues and taken at least 0, earn_taken at most earn_due) holds for every value the code writes, because taken = min(earnDue, max(0, balance)). V5 is a new file in this objective, so editing it does not change the checksum of a shipped migration. releaseRedeem takes the lock before reading priorDue, gives back N minus SUM(redeem_due), and inserts only when the result is positive. Later per-return events see the redeem- row and get 0, so the total given back stays at or below N. All of these paths run under the same per-user advisory lock. The delta adds no new defect and no duplication: the prior-due query was pulled out into priorDue() and reused. The only gap is that evidence.md has no verify run recorded at this SHA.
